questions.stem: Under MPR s. 131, an applicant for Master, Limited (under 60 GT) must provide an appropriate radio operator certificate when:
options: the vessel is equipped with a VHF radiotelephone installation
questions.explanation: The table in MPR s. 131 lists the radio certificate if the vessel has a VHF radiotelephone installation.

questions.stem: A 12 m tug (a towboat) works in sea area A1. Does NSR 2020 s. 204 require a VHF-DSC?
options: No, because it is under 20 m
Yes, because a towboat on a voyage in A1 must carry one
questions.explanation: Section 204 applies to a vessel over 8 m, carrying passengers, or a towboat, on a voyage in A1, within VHF coverage, or more than 5 nm from shore.

questions.stem: Which vessel is excused from the fixed VHF-DSC by s. 204(2)?
options: A vessel carrying six passengers or fewer and not more than 8 m, with a DSC handheld
A vessel with a spare antenna
questions.explanation: The exception is for a vessel that carries six passengers or less and is not more than 8 m, if it has a portable VHF handheld capable of DSC.

questions.stem: On a voyage other than a sheltered waters voyage with a compulsory VHF-DSC, what must the person in charge of the radio watch normally hold?
questions.explanation: MPR s. 266(2) requires the ROC-MC, except for a Near Coastal Class 2 vessel whose VHF is its only radiotelephone, where an ROC-M issued after 1 January 2005 will do.

questions.stem: Which case allows an ROC-M instead of the ROC-MC under MPR s. 266(2)?
options: A Near Coastal Class 2 vessel whose VHF is its only radiotelephone, with an ROC-M issued after 1 January 2005
A tug on a sheltered voyage only
questions.explanation: That is the one stated exception for a voyage other than sheltered waters.

questions.stem: What are the ROC-MC age, validity and pass mark?
options: Age 16, valid 5 years, pass mark 50 percent
Age 21, valid 10 years, pass mark 80 percent
No age limit, valid 1 year, pass mark 60 percent
Minimum age 18, valid for life, pass mark 70 percent
questions.explanation: RIC-25 gives minimum age 18, life validity and a 70 percent pass mark.

questions.stem: Which items must be at the main operating position of the radio installation?
options: The master's certificate of competency only
The RAMN and, where required, the radio inspection certificate
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 212 requires the RAMN and the radio inspection certificate (if s. 240 requires one) at the main operating position; operators' certificates are also kept on board.

questions.stem: Which items does s. 214 require at the main operating position?
options: A spare VHF and a SART
An instruction card such as TP 9878, operating and maintenance instructions, and a visible reliable clock
A copy of the Collision Regulations only
questions.explanation: Section 214 lists the card of distress procedures, instructions and maintenance items, and a visible accurate time device.

questions.stem: Which vessel needs a radio inspection certificate (s. 240)?
options: A passenger vessel on a voyage in sea area A1
A 7 m open boat with no passengers
questions.explanation: Section 240 requires one for a vessel of 20 m or more, a towboat, and a passenger vessel on a voyage in A1 or over 5 nm from shore.

questions.stem: A 22 m vessel has a single VHF-DSC. Which extra items does NSR 2020 require?
options: A NAVTEX receiver in all cases
A spare antenna with cable and an antenna plan
questions.explanation: Section 215 requires a spare antenna for a 20 m or longer vessel with only one VHF-DSC, and s. 213 an antenna plan for 20 m or more.

questions.stem: Who may keep the listening watch or make a navigation safety call on the master's authority?
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 250(1) says the master or a person authorised by the master for these tasks must be a radio operator.
